docs.title: 2. Model parameters
docs.text:
Robust noise estimate. sigma2 for Gaussian fits estimated via median-absolute-deviation of first differences: sigma = 1.4826 * median(|diff(y) - median(diff(y))|) / sqrt(2).

Dataset sigma2 (robust MAD-diff) welllog full 4,674,808.19 welllog stride-8 5,466,698.12 CGH (pooled across 43 subjects) 0.0057

Hyperparameter strategy.

  • welllog: estimate_hyper=True with fixed sigma2. BayesBreakGaussian estimates nu (weighted mean of y) and rho2 (variance of y) from data. Required because welllog values are ~10^5 NMR units; a fixed prior of nu=0, rho2=4.0 places the prior far from the data, collapsing evidence to k_map=1 (see Section 3).
  • CGH: fixed nu=0.0, rho2=4.0. Appropriate for log2-ratio data (neutral copy number at 0, typical CNV excursions up to ±2). Shared prior across 43 subjects.
  • methylation: BetaObs family; hyperparameters estimated by the family from data.

Count priors. geometric_decay_log4 and uniform tested on all primary fits.

BetaObs quadrature. 128 Gauss-Legendre nodes (confirmed sufficient in E08 A4).

CGH pooling. SharedBoundaryReplicatesSegmenter pools 43 subjects: block log-evidences from each subject are summed before the DP; one shared MAP boundary vector is returned.

k_max grid. Primary: {15, 30, 60}. Extended for truncation resolution: - welllog full: up to k_max=100 - welllog stride-8: k_max=60 - CGH single_subject0: up to k_max=100 - methylation: up to k_max=120 (truncation not resolved)

docs.title: 3. Fixes applied before the canonical run
docs.text: Two correctness defects found and fixed during script development. Both affected the superseded run (config SHA256 prefix bae816ac60300df3).

docs.title: Fix 1: _min_len_prior returned 0.0 for valid segments
docs.text: base.py checks if value > 0 and np.isfinite(value). Returning 0.0 caused valid segments to receive -inf in the log-g table. All minimum-length sensitivity cells failed. Fix: return 1.0 for valid segments (log(1.0) = 0.0, no additive penalty), 0.0 for invalid segments (fails > 0 check, assigned -inf).

docs.title: Fix 2: Wrong Gaussian prior for welllog
docs.text: The superseded run used nu=0, rho2=4.0 for welllog. Welllog NMR values are ~10^5; the prior was far from the data. All welllog cells returned k_map=1. Fix: estimate_hyper=True for welllog, letting the model estimate nu and rho2 from data while fixing sigma2 to the robust MAD-diff estimate.

docs.title: 4. Truncation criterion
docs.text: A cell is reported truncated if k_map == k_max OR P(k=k_max|y) >= 0.01. Truncation means substantial posterior mass lies at or above k_max; the unrestricted MAP segment count is unknown. Do not extrapolate a MAP value from a truncated posterior.

docs.title: 6. Boundary marginals
docs.text:
The BayesBreak DP provides exact boundary-event marginals (boundary_marginals_) and boundary location posteriors (boundary_location_posterior_) after fitting, conditional on the MAP segment count. No Markov chain Monte Carlo or variational approximation is required. These are stored as fitted attributes and can be queried for any resolved configuration.

For truncated configurations, boundary marginals conditional on k_map are available but should be interpreted with caution: they condition on a segment count that may not be the unrestricted MAP, and they reflect the boundary distribution within the constrained model support. These are not marginals under the unrestricted model.

Detailed boundary-marginal summaries for the resolved configurations (welllog full geometric_decay_log4 k_max=100, welllog stride-8, welllog min_seg sensitivity, CGH single_subject0) are reported in E09_SCIENTIFIC_STATUS.md.

docs.title: 3. Computational stages and theoretical complexity
docs.text:
Stage Implementation Theoretical complexity Source Block evidence _compute_block_evidence (Gaussian conjugate updates) O(n^2) Nested loop over i, j filling (n+1)x(n+1) array Forward-backward DP _dp.forward_backward O(k_max * n^2) k_max passes, each accumulating n-length prefix sums Posterior over k _dp.posterior_over_k O(k_max * n) Single pass over k, n Boundary marginals _dp.boundary_event_marginals_fixed_k O(k_map * n) k_map-1 outer loops MAP backtracking _dp.max_sum_segmentation O(n + k_map) After max-sum DP O(k_map * n^2) End-to-end est.fit() O(k_max * n^2) Dominated by block evidence + forward-backward

Memory: the block evidence matrix is (n+1) x (n+1) float64 arrays. Forward and backward tables are (k_max+1) x (n+1). Total storage is O(k_max * n + n^2); the O(n^2) block evidence array dominates.

docs.title: 5. Empirical scaling versus theoretical complexity
docs.text:
Slopes fit by log-log OLS across the full n grid at fixed k_max=20:

Stage Observed slope in n Theoretical slope End-to-end 1.16 2 (O(n^2)) Forward-backward 1.14 2 (O(n^2)) Block evidence 2.00 2 (O(n^2)) Peak memory 1.98 2 (O(n^2))

Slope in k_max at fixed n=2048:

Stage Observed slope in k_max Theoretical slope End-to-end 0.89 1 (O(k_max)) Forward-backward 1.01 1 (O(k_max))

Key finding: Memory and block-evidence computation scale as O(n^2) as predicted. Forward-backward scales as O(k_max^1.01 * n^1.14) in practice, substantially better than the theoretical O(k_max * n^2). This is explained by numpy vectorization: the outer loop over k runs in Python (k_max iterations) but the inner sum for each k step is a numpy vector operation of length n, not a Python loop of n iterations. The effective wall-clock cost per forward-backward pass is O(k_max * n) numpy operations rather than O(k_max * n^2) Python iterations, giving empirical exponent closer to 1 than 2 in n.

Do not interpret the empirical slope (1.14 in n) as an asymptotic improvement over the O(n^2) worst-case bound in Proposition~\ref{prop:complexity-paper}. The theoretical bound counts arithmetic operations; the empirical slope reflects numpy's vectorized execution over the measured finite range [128, 2048]. For very large n where the n^2 block matrix no longer fits in CPU cache, the empirical slope may increase toward 2.

docs.title: 6. Memory analysis
docs.text:
Memory scales as O(n^2) (slope 1.98, consistent with 2.0 within measurement noise). At n=2048, peak memory is 500.7 MB, dominated by the (n+1) x (n+1) block evidence array: 2049 x 2049 x 8 bytes = 33.6 MB plus the corresponding (n+1) x (n+1) max-sum array = 67.2 MB. The remaining ~433 MB includes forward/backward tables (k_max * n float64), boundary marginal computations, and Python interpreter overhead.

For conjugate Gaussian: block evidence storage is the primary memory cost. Non-conjugate families with numerical block integration add per-block integration cache overhead but do not change the O(n^2) block table size.

docs.title: 7. Stage time fractions (at n=2048, k_max=20)
docs.text:
Stage Time (s) Fraction of E2E Block evidence 0.103 3.2% Forward-backward 3.023 93.0% Boundary marginals 0.006 0.2% MAP backtracking <0.001 <0.1% Other (setup, post-processing) ~0.116 3.6%

The forward-backward DP is the dominant computation (93% of end-to-end time at n=2048, k_max=20). At smaller n or smaller k_max, block evidence and Python setup contribute proportionally more.

docs.title: 8. Numerical correctness
docs.text: All 15 cells returned k_map=3 (correct: k_true=3 under the generating signal with SNR=2.0 and the geometric-decay prior). No NaN, infinity, or numerical failure occurred. The boundary marginal invariant (sum = k_map - 1 = 2) was verified in the supplemental boundary marginals run for welllog configurations.

docs.title: 9. Comparison with existing runtime measurements
docs.text:
The manuscript section "Finite-range runtime behavior" reports existing measurements at n in {50,...,400} with k_max in {10, 20}. At k_max=20, n=400: ~0.77s (from existing chart). The E10 benchmark at n=512, k_max=20: 0.62s. These are from different hardware and timing setups; the comparison is illustrative, not a controlled regression.

The fitted log-log slopes from existing measurements were ~1.07 (k_max=10) and ~1.14 (k_max=20) in n, consistent with the E10 slope of 1.14 (k_max=20) from this benchmark.

docs.title: Real-data showcase¶
docs.text:
Four real-data case studies fit by BayesBreak, mirroring §6 of the manuscript:

  1. Well-log NMR geology (Gaussian block, length 4050 NMR series).
  2. Coriell array-CGH copy number (heteroscedastic multi-subject Gaussian).
  3. S&P 500 squared returns (Gaussian on log r_t^2). Note: S&P 500 is excluded from the confirmed E09 real-data analysis (live data unavailable; see §6). This notebook demonstrates the segmenter on a simulated analog that matches the statistical structure. Never interpret simulated SPX results as genuine market-regime evidence.
  4. methylKit CpG methylation (Beta-response block with per-CpG precision).

Each loader falls back to a deterministic simulated analog when the network download is unavailable, so this notebook runs end-to-end on a fresh checkout without any datasets installed.

docs.title: Diagnostics walkthrough¶
docs.text: All four bayesbreak.diagnostics routines on one synthetic Bernoulli-logistic dataset.

docs.title: 1. DP invariants (run_dp_diagnostics)¶
docs.text: Checks ∑ P(k) = 1, forward/backward agreement (prop:fb-duality), ∑_i P(b_i | y, k_map) = k_map − 1, and MAP backtrack consistency (thm:map-correctness).

docs.title: 2. Non-conjugate diagnostics (run_non_conjugate_diagnostics)¶
docs.text: Measures the empirical ε of ass:uniform-block-error and the worst-case TV bound exp(2 k_max ε) − 1 from cor:probability-error-conversion. Reference fit uses high-Q Gauss–Hermite quadrature.

docs.title: 3. Prior-sensitivity (run_prior_sensitivity)¶
docs.text: Reruns the DP under perturbations of p(k) and the length factor g(ℓ); reports Δ p(k|y) and Δ P(b_i|y, k_map) per variant. This is the §5b partition-prior sensitivity diagnostic.

docs.title: 4. Held-out G-selection (select_n_groups_by_holdout)¶
docs.text: K-fold marginal log-likelihood over the sequence axis for the latent- template mixture. Mitigates rem:teicher-overspec (overspecified-G redundancy).

Run BayesBreak alongside the upstream-driven baseline wrappers in bayesbreak.baselines. We do not re-implement these algorithms — each call is a thin wrapper around the canonical package.

docs.title: Sliding-window decomposition for large n¶
docs.text:
The exact DP is Θ(k_max n²) time and at least Θ(k_max n) memory (prop:bb-complexity). At n ≳ 10^5 this becomes impractical. §5b Computational regime proposes a sliding-window decomposition that splits the sequence into overlapping windows, runs the exact DP on each, and stitches the per-window outputs.

This is an approximation — stitched results do not inherit thm:dp-correctness exactly and the boundary-event-sum identity holds only per window.

docs.title: When to prefer the exact DP¶
docs.text: Use the sliding-window when n would make prop:bb-complexity time or memory prohibitive (typically n ≳ 10^5). For smaller n, the exact DP gives you the boundary-event sum identity, the forward-backward duality, and Corollary cor:probability-error-conversion exactly.

docs.title: Latent-group EM¶
docs.text: Subjects come from G unknown groups, each with its own boundary template. BayesBreakMixtureClassifier alternates E-step (exact responsibilities) and M-step (responsibility-weighted max-sum DP), optimising the finite template-mixture objective ℓ_⋆ (thm:em-monotone).

docs.title: Fit the mixture with G=2 (correct G)¶
Verify identifiability anchoring (prop:latent-identifiability)¶
docs.text: The canonical anchor sorts groups by k_g, then lexicographically by t^{(g)}. Two restarts converging to the same template multiset must report them in identical order.

docs.title: Held-out G selection (select_n_groups_by_holdout)¶
docs.text: Mitigates rem:teicher-overspec overspecification: at G > G*, two distinct (π, τ) tuples can produce identical mixture densities. Held-out marginal log-likelihood is the §5b recommended response.

docs.title: Core dynamic-programming verification¶
docs.text:
This notebook turns the central BayesBreak Gaussian workflow into an inspectable verification report. It checks public interfaces, dynamic-programming invariants, posterior normalization, MAP reconstruction, prediction behavior, prior sensitivity, edge cases, and small-scale runtime trends.

The synthetic boundaries are known because this is a controlled software check. Agreement on these data is not a universal accuracy claim. When executed, the notebook writes diagnostics to results/notebook_verification/core_dp/.

docs.title: 1–3. Configure, load, and create deterministic fixtures¶
docs.text: The environment cell fixes the random seed, records dependency versions, and creates a dedicated output directory. The fixture below has three Gaussian regimes with true boundaries at indices 35 and 70. A shuffled negative control preserves the marginal distribution while removing the ordered regime structure.

docs.title: 4. Inspect components and public interfaces¶
docs.text: Before fitting, inspect constructor and method signatures directly. This catches accidental API drift while keeping the notebook tied to public objects rather than implementation internals.

docs.title: 5–6. Run checks and capture structured results¶
docs.text: record_check keeps pass/fail/error status, expected and observed values, execution time, and tracebacks. The estimator is fitted once, then the notebook verifies posterior normalization, evidence-table shape, admissibility, MAP reconstruction, predictions, segment labels, score, and sklearn cloning.

docs.title: 7. Inspect posterior state and DP diagnostics¶
docs.text: The four panels connect raw data to the stored computational objects. The evidence heatmap displays only finite admissible blocks. The diagnostic report independently checks posterior normalization, forward/backward duality, the boundary-event sum, and MAP backtracking consistency.

docs.title: 8. Analyze prior sensitivity and a negative control¶
docs.text: Prior variants are perturbations, not alternative truths. The shuffled control preserves all response values but destroys their sequence order. Comparing posterior summaries reveals sequence sensitivity without claiming the fitted shuffled partition is ground truth.

docs.title: 9–10. Measure and plot performance¶
docs.text: Exact segmentation stores an $O(n^2)$ block-evidence table. This small benchmark uses three repeats per size and reports median runtime, interquartile range, throughput, and evidence-table memory. It is a local diagnostic, not a cross-machine benchmark.

docs.title: 11. Analyze errors and edge cases¶
docs.text: Expected failures are successful contract checks only when both exception type and message fragment match. This section covers an invalid segment budget, nonfinite observations, mismatched lengths, and prediction before fitting.

docs.title: 12. Generate the verification report¶
docs.text: The final cell combines invariant checks, built-in diagnostics, and expected-failure contracts. It exports machine-readable tables and an at-a-glance status chart. Re-running the notebook replaces only files in its dedicated report directory.

docs.title: Likelihood-family and prediction verification¶
docs.text:
This notebook inspects BayesBreak's concrete likelihood families on deterministic synthetic signals, compares MAP segmentations, verifies posterior predictive densities against analytic references, and records support violations as expected outcomes.

When executed, this tutorial writes outputs to results/notebook_verification/families/. Family comparisons illustrate software behavior on controlled fixtures; they are not evidence that one family is universally preferable.

docs.title: 1. Inspect the family factory and prediction interface¶
docs.text: The factory provides aliases for concrete estimators. Posterior prediction routes new observations through each fitted family's posterior_predictive_logpdf_block implementation, so unsupported families must fail explicitly rather than falling back to a Gaussian density.

docs.title: 2. Create family-specific fixtures and fit the models¶
docs.text: All fixtures contain one change at index 40 but obey different supports. Binomial trial counts are explicit descriptors, and Beta observations remain strictly inside $(0,1)$.

docs.title: 3. Visualize MAP signals and posterior segment counts¶
docs.text: Rows align the observed support, fitted MAP signal, declared boundary, and posterior over segment count. The axes intentionally differ by family because their response scales are not commensurate.

docs.title: 4. Verify posterior prediction against analytic references¶
docs.text: These checks isolate one fitted segment so the conjugate posterior is available in closed form. Bernoulli uses Beta–Bernoulli prediction, Binomial uses the Beta-Binomial PMF with explicit new-trial descriptors, and fractional Beta uses the declared Beta density.

docs.title: 5. Plot posterior predictive distributions¶
docs.text: The plots show actual predictive mass or density, obtained by exponentiating the verified log scores. Binomial predictions condition on the displayed number of new trials.

docs.title: 6. Capture support and unsupported-operation failures¶
docs.text: Support checks are part of scientific correctness: binary data cannot silently become fractional, Binomial trial descriptors must be positive integers, Beta observations cannot be clipped onto the boundary, and logistic-normal posterior prediction is explicitly unimplemented.

docs.title: 7. Compare runtime and generate the report¶
docs.text: Runtime is shown only for these matched-size fixtures and this machine. The final report combines fitted-model checks, analytic prediction error, and expected support failures.

docs.title: Advanced models and comparator verification¶
docs.text:
This notebook inspects multivariate shared/independent segmentation, pooled replicate evidence, sliding-window approximation, supervised grouped classification, latent-template mixtures, and normalized comparator wrappers.

Each section states its estimand. Shared, independent, latent, and baseline outputs are fitted methods—not external truth. Controlled synthetic boundaries and labels are used only where explicitly declared.

docs.title: 1. Shared versus independent multivariate segmentation¶
docs.text: Three channels share declared boundaries at 30 and 65 but differ in scale and noise. The shared model estimates one partition; the independent model estimates a partition per channel. Both are scored against the same declared boundaries.

docs.title: 2. Verify pooled replicate evidence¶
docs.text: For conditionally independent replicate sequences with common boundaries, pooled block log evidence must equal the sum of per-subject block log evidences when all fits use the same fixed hyperparameters.

docs.title: 3. Inspect sliding-window approximation¶
docs.text: The wrapper is exact only when the full sequence fits inside one window. On a long signal it stitches overlapping local fits, so this section checks finite outputs and recovery near a well-separated declared boundary without claiming global-DP equivalence.

docs.title: 4. Supervised groups and latent mixtures¶
docs.text: Known-group classification uses declared labels. The mixture fit does not know those labels; its component indices are permutation-invariant, so evaluation aligns fitted components to declared groups with a maximum-overlap assignment. The aligned score is a controlled-fixture diagnostic, not proof of latent identifiability.

docs.title: 5. Normalize and compare baseline outputs¶
docs.text: Comparator wrappers return one schema regardless of upstream implementation. All methods below see the same clean three-regime signal and are scored against the same declared boundaries with the same tolerance. Method agreement is not labeled external truth.

docs.title: 6. Generate the advanced-model report¶
docs.text: The report records structural invariants, controlled-fixture metrics, and local timings. It does not collapse methods into a single ranking because they target different modeling assumptions.
